title: Mathematics books
text:
These math books are recommended by Art of Problem Solving administrators and members of the AoPS Community.

Levels of reading and math ability are loosely defined as follows:

  • Elementary is for elementary school students up through possibly early middle school (MOEMS and similar contests).
  • Getting Started is recommended for students who are participating in contests like AMC 8/10/12 and MATHCOUNTS.
  • Intermediate is recommended for students who can at least get close to passing the AMC 10/12.
  • Olympiad is recommended for high school students who can at least come close to qualifying for the USA(J)MO.
  • Collegiate is recommended for college and university students. This is often split between undergraduate and graduate levels.

Before adding any books to this page, please review the AoPS Wiki:Linking books page.

Books By Subject[edit]

General Introduction / Multiple Topics[edit]

Elementary[edit]

  • Mathematical Circle Diaries, Year 1: Complete Curriculum for Grades 5 to 7 by Anna Burago.
  • Mathematical Circle Diaries, Year 2: Complete Curriculum for Grades 6 to 8 by Anna Burago.
  • Math Circles for Elementary School Students by Natasha Rozhkovskaya.
  • Problems to Solve in Primary School Mathematics by Bruce Henry, Lorraine J. Mottershead, Andy R. Edwards, Janine McIntosh, Anna Nakos, Katrina Sims, Alice Thomas, and Giovanna Vardaro.
  • Number Sense Magic by Leo Ramirez.
  • Math Circle by the Bay: Topics for Grades 1–5 by Laura Givental, Maria Nemirovskaya, and Ilya Zakharevich.
  • 100 Challenging Maths Problems
  • mathleague.org 4th and 5th Grade Practice Packet by Sonya Land.

Getting Started[edit]

  • Getting Started with Competition Math, a book meant for true beginners (on-target middle school students, or advanced elementary school students). It is written by AoPS Community Member cargeek9, currently a college student. It covers the basics of algebra, geometry, combinatorics, and number theory, along with sets of accompanying practice problems at the end of every section.
  • AoPS publishes Richard Rusczyk's, David Patrick's, and Ravi Boppana's Prealgebra textbook, which is recommended for advanced elementary and middle school students.
  • AoPS publishes Competition Math for Middle School by Jason Batterson, who also was an author of the Beast Academy series.
  • Math Leads for Mathletes Book 1 by Titu Andreescu and Branislav Kisacanin.
  • Math Leads for Mathletes Book 2 by Titu Andreescu and Branislav Kisacanin.
  • First Steps for Problem Solvers by Mary Teresa Fyfe and Andrew Jobbings.
  • Problems to Solve in Middle School Mathematics Book 1 by Bruce Henry, Lorraine J. Mottershead, Andy R. Edwards, Janine McIntosh, Anna Nakos, Katrina Sims, Alice Thomas, and Giovanna Vardaro.
  • Problem to Solve in Middle School Mathematics Book 2 by Bruce Henry and K. McAvaney.
  • Hard Math For Middle School: IMLEM Edition by Glenn Ellison.
  • Hard Math For Middle School: IMLEM Plus Edition by Glenn Ellison. This is basically the above plus a chapter with more advanced topics for School and basic Chapter-level MathCounts.
  • Hard Math For Middle School: Workbook by Glenn Ellison.
  • Problem Solving: Exploring Paths Less Traveled by Richard Grassl and Tabitha Mingus.

Algebra[edit]

Getting Started[edit]

  • AoPS publishes Richard Rusczyk's Introduction to Algebra textbook, which is recommended for advanced elementary, middle, and high school students.
  • Algebra: For The Enthusiastic Beginner by David Morin
  • Challenging Problems in Algebra by Alfred S. Posamentier and Charles T. Salkind.
  • Mathematics via Problems: Part 1: Algebra by Arkadiy Skopenkov.
  • Introduction to Algebra by Jeremy D. King.
  • Algebra by I.M. Gelfand and Alexander Shen.

Intermediate[edit]

  • AoPS publishes Richard Rusczyk's and Mathew Crawford's Intermediate Algebra textbook, which is recommended for advanced middle and high school students.
  • Complex Numbers from A to ...Z by Titu Andreescu
  • 105 Algebra Problems from the AMSP by Titu Andreescu.
  • 108 Algebra Problems from the AMY by Titu Andreescu and Adithya Ganesh.
  • Ten Themes in Algebra for Mathematics Competitions by Titu Andreescu and Alessandro Ventullo.
  • 114 Exponent and Logarithm Problems from the AMSP by Titu Andreescu and Sean Elliott.
  • Attacking Problems in Logarithms and Exponential Functions by David S. Kahn.

Olympiad[edit]

  • Introduction to Functional Equations by Costas Efthimiou.
  • 124 Challenging Algebra Problems + 30 Bonus Problems by Titu Andreescu and Alessandro Ventullo. Don't underestimate the difficulty of the problems by the chapter topics. The problems are Olympiad-level.
  • 120 Awesome Algebra Problems + 20 Bonus Problems by Titu Andreescu and Alessandro Ventullo. Don't underestimate the difficulty of the problems by the chapter topics. The problems are very much like olympiads.
  • 117 Polynomial Problems from the AMSP by Titu Andreescu, Navid Safaei, and Alessandro Ventullo. This book is the first book in a three-part series on Olympiad polynomial problems, which includes the book below.
  • Awesome Polynomials for Mathematics Competitions by Titu Andreescu, Navid Safaei, and Alessandro Ventullo. Contains 252 examples, 105 end of chapter problems, and 77 additional problems. This book is the second book in a three-part series on Olympiad polynomial problems, which includes the book above.
  • Selection Tests in Algebra for Mathematical Olympiads by Corneliu Manescu-Avram.
  • 101 Problems in Algebra from the Training of the USA IMO Team by Titu Andreescu and Zuming Feng
  • Al-Jabr: Higher Algebraic Yield by Hatem al-Ani, Ali al-Ani, and Yousuf Wameedh.

Linear Algebra[edit]

Computational[edit]

  • Introduction to Linear Algebra by Gilbert Strang.

Proof Based[edit]

  • Linear Algebra Done Right by Sheldon Axler.

Abstract Algebra[edit]

Collegiate[edit]

Undergraduate[edit]
  • Abstract Algebra by David S. Dummit and Richard M. Foote. This is a famous textbook, and is usually the go-to book for students wishing to learn about groups, rings, fields and their properties.
  • Undergraduate Algebra by Serge Lang. Some compare it to being similar to Dummit and Foote with regards to rigor, although this text is slightly more terse.
  • Basic Algebra I by Nathan Jacobson -- Contains harder and more interesting problems than Dummit and Foote. Assumes a decent coverage of Linear Algebra
  • Integer and Polynomial Algebra by Kenneth R. Davidson and Matthew Satriano.
  • Abstract Algebra: Theory and Applications by Thomas W. Judson.
Graduate[edit]
  • Basic Algebra II by Nathan Jacobson -- A continuation of Jacobson's first volume.
  • Algebra by Serge Lang -- Extends undergraduate Abstract Algebra to the graduate level by studying homological algebra and more.
  • Algebra: A Graduate Course by I. Martin Isaacs.
  • Algebra by Thomas W. Hungerford.
  • Introduction to Lie Algebras: Finite and Infinite Dimension by J. I. Hall.
  • Algebra: Chapter 0 by Paolo Aluffi.
  • Finite Group Theory by I. Martin Isaacs.

Calculus[edit]

Single Variable/AP (Intermediate)[edit]

  • The Hitchhiker's Guide to Calculus by Michael Spivak.
  • Calculus Made Easy by Silvanus P. Thompson.
  • AoPS publishes Dr. David Patrick's Calculus textbook, which is recommended for advanced middle and high school students.
  • Calculus: Volume I by Tom M. Apostol -- Provides a good transition into linear algebra which is uncommon in single variable calculus texts.
  • Single Variable Calculus by James Stewart, Daniel K. Clegg and Saleem Watson -- Contains plenty of exercises for practice and focuses on application rather than rigor.
  • Calculus by Michael Spivak. Top students swear by this book.
  • Honors Calculus by Charles R. MacCluer -- Uses the topological definition of the limit rather than the traditional delta-epsilon approach.
  • Calculus of One Variable by Joseph W. Kitchen. A well-respected treatment of one variable calculus, this book also covers plane analytic geometry and infinite series.

Multivariable (Collegiate)[edit]

  • Multivariable Calculus by James Stewart, Daniel K. Clegg, and Saleem Watson.
  • Calculus: Volume II by Tom M. Apostol.
  • Advanced Calculus of Several Variables by C.H. Edwards.
  • Vector Calculus by Peter Baxandall and Hans Liebeck.

Differential Equations[edit]

  • Elementary Differential Equations by C. Henry Edwards and David E. Penney

Analysis[edit]

Collegiate[edit]

Undergraduate[edit]
  • Understanding Analysis by Stephen Abbott.
  • Principles of Mathematical Analysis by Walter Rudin. Affectionately called "Baby Rudin" by some, Principles of Mathematical Analysis is known to be very terse for the analysis layman.
  • Analysis I by Terrence Tao -- An easier first read than Rudin, and it provides plenty of examples with thorough explanations.
  • Analysis II by Terrence Tao -- Continues off from where Volume I ended and finishes at the Lebesgue Integral.
  • Elementary Analysis: The Theory of Calculus by Kenneth A. Ross.
  • Real Analysis by Rami Shakarchi and Elias M. Stein.
  • Complex Analysis by Rami Shakarchi and Elias M. Stein.
Graduate[edit]
  • Real and Complex Analysis by Walter Rudin. Called "Papa Rudin" by some, Real and Complex Analysis is typically used at the graduate level.
  • Functional Analysis by Rami Shakarchi and Elias M. Stein.

Combinatorics[edit]

Getting Started[edit]

  • AoPS publishes Dr. David Patrick's Introduction to Counting & Probability textbook, which is recommended for advanced middle and high school students.
  • 112 Combinatorial Problems from AMSP is a great discrete math book covering topics ranging from permutations and combinations to using creativity to count to doing proofs and then gives exposure to advanced topics like probability theory. Great for AMC 8/10/12
  • Mathematics via Problems: Part 3: Combinatorics by Mikhail B. Skopenkov and Alexey A. Zaslavky.
  • Introduction to Combinatorics by Gerry Leversha and Dominic Rowland.

Intermediate[edit]

  • AoPS publishes Dr. David Patrick's Intermediate Counting & Probability textbook, which is recommended for advanced middle and high school students.
  • Mathematics of Choice by Ivan Niven.
  • CleverMath Combinatorics by Titu Andreescu.
  • Combinatorial Problems in Mathematical Competitions by Yao Zhang.
  • Topics in Combinatorics by Gerry Leversha and Dominic Rowland.

Olympiad[edit]

Lower[edit]
  • Counting Rocks! An Introduction to Combinatorics by Henry Adams, Kelly Emmrich, Maria Gillespie, Shannon Golden, and Rachel Pries.
  • Problem-Solving Methods in Combinatorics: An Approach to Olympiad Problems by Pablo Soberon.
  • An Exploration of Olympiad Combinatorics by Rushil Mathur.
Upper[edit]
  • 102 Combinatorial Problems From the Training of the USA IMO Team by Titu Andreescu and Zuming Feng.
  • Graphs: An Introduction by Radu Bumbacea.
  • Olympiad Combinatorics by Pranav A. Sriram.

Collegiate[edit]

Undergraduate[edit]
Discrete Math (general)[edit]
  • Discrete Mathematics - An Open Introduction by Oscar Levin. Also covers mathematical logic, polynomials, and introductory number theory.
Applied Combinatorics/Statistics[edit]
  • Attacking Probability and Statistics Problems by David S. Kahn.
  • Applied Combinatorics by Fred Roberts and Barry Tesman.
  • Applied Combinatorics by Alan Tucker.
  • A First Course in Probability by Sheldon Ross
  • Probability: For the Enthusiastic Beginner by David Morin (some problems involve calculus).
  • generatingfunctionology by Herbert S. Wilf.
Introductory[edit]
  • Introductory Combinatorics by Richard A. Brualdi.
  • Introductory Combinatorics by Kenneth P. Bogart
  • Combinatorics Through Guided Discovery by Kenneth P. Bogart, Mitchel T. Keller, Oscar Levin, and Kent E. Morrison.
  • Principles and Techniques in Combinatorics by Chuan Chong Chen and Khee Meng Koh and Solutions Manual by Kean Pew Foo and Mingyan Simon Lin.
  • Combinatorics and Graph Theory by John M. Harris, Jeffry L. Hirst, and Michael Mossinghoff.
  • Combinatorics: Topics, Techniques, Algorithms by Peter Cameron.
  • A Path to Combinatorics for Undergraduates: Counting Strategies by Titu Andreescu and Zuming Feng.
Advanced Undergraduate/Beginning Graduate[edit]
  • Enumerative Combinatorics, Volume 1 by Richard Stanley.
  • Enumerative Combinatorics, Volume 2 by Richard Stanley.
  • Algebraic Combinatorics by Richard Stanley.
  • A Walk Through Combinatorics by Miklos Bona.
  • Exploring Combinatorial Mathematics by Richard Grassl and Oscar Levin.
Graduate[edit]
  • Graph Theory by J.A. Bondy and U.S.R. Murty.
  • Graph Theory by Reinhard Diestel.
  • Advanced Graph Theory by Santosh Kumar Yadav.
  • Modern Graph Theory by Bela Bollobas.
  • Lessons in Enumerative Combinatorics by Omer Egecioglu and Adriano M. Garsia.
  • Integration and Probability by Paul Malliavin.
  • Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups by Anders Bjorner and Francesco Brenti.
  • A Course in Enumeration by Martin Aigner.
  • Combinatorics and Commutative Algebra by Richard Stanley.
  • Combinatorics: The Art of Counting by Bruce E. Sagan.
  • Combinatorial Reciprocity Theorems: An Invitation to Enumerative Geometric Combinatorics by Matthias Beck and Raman Sanyal.
  • The Probabilistic Method by Noga Alon and Joel H. Spencer.

Geometry[edit]

Getting Started[edit]

  • AoPS publishes Richard Rusczyk's Introduction to Geometry textbook, which is recommended for advanced middle and high school students.
  • Mathematics via Problems: Part 2: Geometry by Alexey A. Zaslavky and Mikhail B. Skopenkov.
  • Geometry by I.M. Gelfand and Tatiana Alexeyevskaya.
  • 106 Geometry Problems from the AwesomeMath Summer Program by Titu Andreescu, Michal Rolinek, and Josef Tkadlec

Intermediate[edit]

  • Challenging Problems in Geometry -- A good book for students who already have a solid handle on elementary geometry.
  • New Problems in Euclidean Geometry by David Monk.
  • Solving Problems in Geometry: Insights and Strategies for Mathematical Olympiad and Competitions by Kim Hoo Hang and Haibin Wang.
  • Advanced Euclidean Geometry by Roger A. Johnson.

Olympiad[edit]

Lower (Upper Intermediate)[edit]
  • Plane Euclidean Geometry: Theory and Problems by A.D. Gardiner and CJ Bradley.
  • 107 Geometry Problems from the AwesomeMath Year-Round Program Titu Andreescu, Michal Rolinek, and Josef Tkadlec
  • Geometry Revisited -- A classic. Covers mostly theory, with scattered problems.
  • Introduction to Olympiad Geometry by Waldemar Pompe.
Upper[edit]
  • Euclidean Geometry in Mathematical Olympiads by Evan Chen
  • Projective Geometry by H.S.M. Coxeter.
  • Lemmas in Olympiad Geometry by Titu Andreescu, Cosmin Pohoata, and Sam Korsky.
  • 110 Geometry Problems for the International Mathematical Olympiad by Titu Andreescu and Cosmin Pohoata.
  • The Geometry of Remarkable Elements by Constantin Mihalescu, edited by Titu Andreescu, Dorin Andrica, Paul Blaga, and Dan Branzei.
  • Regular Polygons by Djura Paunic.

Collegiate[edit]

  • Geometry: A Comprehensive Course by Dan Pedoe.
  • Non-Euclidean Geometry by H.S.M. Coxeter. This treatment can be enjoyed by anyone who is familiar with algebra up to the elements of group theory.
  • College Geometry: An Introduction to the Modern Geometry of the Triangle and the Circle by Nathan Altshiller-Court.

Topology[edit]

Collegiate[edit]

  • Topology by James Munkres. Topology is arguably the most renowned topology textbook of all time. It also contains an excellent introduction to set theory and logic. A free version can be found here.
  • Elementary Topology by Michael C. Gemignani.

Differential[edit]

  • Introduction to Smooth Manifolds by John M. Lee.

Inequalities[edit]

Intermediate[edit]

  • An Introduction to Inequalities by Edwin Beckenbach.
  • Geometric Inequalities by Nicholas D. Kazarinoff
  • 109 Inequalities from the AMSP by Titu Andreescu and Adithya Ganesh.
  • Introduction to Inequalities by CJ Bradley.

Olympiad[edit]

Lower[edit]
  • Inequalities: A Mathematical Olympiad Approach by Manfrino, Ortega, and Delgado.
  • 116 Algebraic Inequalities from the AMY by Titu Andreescu and Marius Stanean.
  • 113 Geometric Inequalities from the AMSP by Adrian Andreescu, Titu Andreescu, and Oleg Mushkarov.
  • 118 Inequalities for Mathematics Competitions by Titu Andreescu and Marius Stanean.
Upper[edit]
  • 122 Challenging Inequalities by Titu Andreescu and Marius Stanean.
  • New, Newer, and Newest Inequalities by Titu Andreescu and Marius Stanean.
  • Advanced Olympiad Inequalities by Alijadallah Belabess.

Collegiate[edit]

  • Inequalities by G. H. Hardy, J. E. Littlewood, and G. Polya.
  • Algebraic Inequalities: New Vistas by Titu Andreescu and Mark Saul.
  • The Cauchy-Schwarz Master Class: An Introduction to the Art of Mathematical Inequalities by J. Michael Steele. The text is accessible to anyone who knows calculus and who cares about solving problems. It is well suited to self-study, directed study, or as a supplement to courses in analysis, probability, and combinatorics.
  • Geometric Problems on Maxima and Minima by Titu Andreescu, Oleg Mushkarov, and Luchezar Stoyanov. Ideal for use at the junior and senior undergraduate level, as well as in enrichment programs and Olympiad training for advanced high school students, this book’s breadth and depth will appeal to a wide audience, from secondary school teachers and pupils to graduate students, professional mathematicians, and puzzle enthusiasts.

Number Theory[edit]

Getting Started[edit]

  • The AoPS Introduction to Number Theory by Mathew Crawford.
  • Introduction to Number Theory by CJ Bradley.
  • 121 Number Theory Problems for Mathematics Competitions by Titu Andreescu and Alessandro Ventullo. Contains lectures and problems from AwesomeMath's Level 1 Number Theory summer program.

Intermediate[edit]

  • Number Theory: Structures, Examples, and Problems by Titu Andreescu and Dorin Andrica.
  • Introduction to Number Theory in Mathematics Contests Book 1 by Titu Andreescu and Marian Tetiva.
  • Introduction to Number Theory in Mathematics Contests Book 2 by Titu Andreescu and Marian Tetiva.

Olympiad[edit]

Lower[edit]
  • Olympiad Number Theory by Justin Stevens. Considered one of the best resources for preparing for number theory in mathematical competitions.
  • Problems of Number Theory in Mathematical Competitions by Yu Hongbing, translated by Lin Lei.
Upper[edit]
  • Modern Olympiad Number Theory by Aditya Khurmi.
  • Number Theory: Concepts and Problems by Titu Andreescu, Gabriel Dospinescu, and Oleg Mushkarov.
  • 104 Number Theory Problems from the Training of the USA IMO Team by Titu Andreescu, Dorin Andrica, and Zuming Feng.
  • Selection Tests in Number Theory for Mathematical Olympiads by Corneliu Manescu-Avram.

Collegiate[edit]

  • Elementary Number Theory by David M. Burton
  • Quadratic Diophantine Equations by Titu Andreescu and Dorin Andrica.
  • Explorations in Number Theory by Cam McLeman, Erin McNicholas, and Colin Starr.
  • A Textbook of Algebraic Number Theory by Sudesh Kaur Khanduja.
  • Excursions in Multiplicative Number Theory by Olivier Ramare.
  • An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers by G. H. Hardy, Edward M. Wright, and Andrew Wiles (6th Edition).
  • Number Theory by George E. Andrews.

Trigonometry[edit]

Intermediate[edit]

  • Trigonometry by I.M. Gelfand and Mark Saul.
  • Trigonometry: A Clever Study Guide by James Tanton.

Olympiad[edit]

  • 103 Trigonometry Problems by Titu Andreescu and Zuming Feng.
  • 115 Trigonometry Problems from the AMSP by Titu Andreescu and Vlad Crisan.
  • 119 Trigonometry Problems for Mathematics Competitions by Titu Andreescu and Alessandro Ventullo.

Problem Solving[edit]

Getting Started[edit]

  • the Art of Problem Solving Volume 1 by Sandor Lehoczky and Richard Rusczyk is recommended for avid math students in grades 7-9.
  • Mathematical Circles: Russian Experience -- A wonderful peek into Russian math training.
  • 100 Great Problems of Elementary Mathematics by Heinrich Dorrie.
  • A Decade of the Berkeley Math Circle: The American Experience, Volume I by Zvezdelina Stankova and Tom Rike.
  • A Decade of the Berkeley Math Circle: The American Experience, Volume II by Zvezdelina Stankova and Tom Rike.
  • A Moscow Math Circle: Week-by-Week Problem Sets by Sergey Dorichenko.
  • How to Solve It by George Polya.

Intermediate[edit]

  • the Art of Problem Solving Volume 2 by Sandor Lehoczky and Richard Rusczyk is recommended for avid math students in grades 9-12.
  • A Mathematical Mosaic by Putnam Fellow Ravi Vakil.
  • Solving Mathematical Problems: A Personal Perspective by Terence Tao.
  • Invitation to a Mathematical Festival by Ivan Yashchenko.
  • A Problem Solver's Handbook by Andrew Jobbings.

Olympiad[edit]

  • Mathematical Olympiad Challenges by Titu Andreescu and Razvan Gelca.
  • Mathematical Olympiad Treasures by Titu Andreescu and Bogdan Enescu.
  • Mathematical Miniatures by Titu Andreescu and Svetoslav Savchev.
  • Problem Solving Tactics by Pasquale, Do, and Mathews.
  • Problem Solving Strategies by Arthur Engel.
  • Problems from the Book, 3rd Edition by Titu Andreescu and Gabriel Dospinescu.

Collegiate[edit]

  • How to Think Like a Mathematician by Kevin Houston.
  • Problem Solving Through Problems by Loren Larson. The book serves as an introduction and guide to the problem literature (e.g., as found in the problems sections of undergraduate mathematics journals) and as an easily accessed reference of essential knowledge for students and teachers of mathematics.
  • The Art and Craft of Problem Solving by Paul Zeitz, former coach of the U.S. math team. Contains sections on graph theory and calculus.
